newsitem.title: SENEGAL: World Bank head urges Africa to embrace technology.
newsitem.headline: World Bank head urges Africa to embrace technology.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn told business leaders in Senegal on Sunday that they and government must embrace the use of computers and the Internet to propel the continent into the 21st century.

"It's important for the government and the private sector to enter the 21st century with technology such as Internet and computers," he told journalists after talks with business leaders in the capital Dakar.
Wolfensohn arrived in Senegal on Saturday at the start of a nine-day African tour that will also take him to Ghana, Mozambique and South Africa.

Before leaving Washington, he said African nations were making real economic progress and that he wanted to build on that success. "What is most needed is to find a way to bring in private investments in this country," he said on arrival.
On Sunday, he inaugurated new offices in Senegal of the International Finance Corporation, the World Bank subsidiary that will fund activities of the private sector.
During talks with donor representatives he stressed that good governance was essential for development.
Wolfensohn chose Africa for his first trip following his appointment in 1995. He travels to Ghana on Monday.
